value.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for reviewing a repository, site or video on a rotation, run after run
value.lets_workers: Cut a repository, site or video into scopes with the checks each needs from other packs; propose a review schedule that waits for a person's approval; pick the next scopes by a fixed rule from what was reviewed least recently or changed most; diff each run's findings against the last run of the same scope, so new, still open, fixed, unverified, unexplained, unchecked and reopened findings are told apart; propose the fix, verification and reproduction each one needs, with a different worker verifying; keep a review log that shows coverage over time; and review one's own change before handing it on.

flow.when: Once per target, and again when its structure changes.
A person approves the schedule, with an expiry; until then nothing runs on it.
Each approved window, or by hand.
After the picked scope's checks report.
A different worker verifies every fix the diff finds unverified.
Before a worker hands any change on.

complements: The checks themselves belong to other packs, such as codebase health review, edge and corner cases, accessibility audit, screenshot design review, video QA, annoyance hunt and wiring and conformance checks; this pack decides which scope runs when and what changed since last time.
Findings, fixes, independent verification and guards come from the findings to fixes pack; a cause that keeps coming back goes to its review-patterns.
The person's approval reuses the unattended run record pack's run approval, and an unattended window follows its run guards.
Comparing measured numbers with an accepted baseline is the regression watch pack; this pack compares findings with the last run.

value.title: How a repository, site or video is reviewed on a rotation, run after run
value.category_reason: A reusable procedure with guardrails, followed by every verb in this pack.
lifecycle: map-scopes cuts the target into scopes, names each scope's checks from other packs, and proposes a review schedule.
approve-schedule is a person's verb: until it is recorded, the schedule is only a proposal and nothing runs on it.
pick-scope applies the rotation rule to the review log and proposes the picked scopes' checks, at most ten verbs per pick.
The checks run as their own packs' verbs, each with its own receipt.

diff-against-last-run compares this run's findings with the last run of the same scope and sorts each into new, still open, fixed, gone without verification, gone unexplained, not checked or reopened.
log-run appends the run to the review log by compare-and-set, so coverage over time stays visible.
review-coverage reads the log across a window for scopes left out, checks that never fail or never run, and causes that keep coming back.
review-own-change is the self-review a worker runs on its own change before handing it to a different worker.
rules: A schedule is a proposal until a person approves it, with scopes, an allowance and an expiry.
Gone is not fixed: a finding is fixed only when a fix is recorded and a worker other than the fixer verified it.
A check that did not run is not a pass; the findings it would have seen stay open as not checked.
Diff only like with like: the same scope and the same check versions as the last run.
A finding seen again after it was closed is reopened, and its guard failed to catch it, so a stronger guard is proposed.
Self-review comes first and is never the last word: the worker that made a change never approves or verifies it.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; they never enqueue.

value.title: Picking the next scopes: least recently reviewed or changed most
value.category_reason: A zero-call rule: the same log, catalog and churn always pick the same scopes.
order: Scopes never reviewed come first, in catalog order.
Urgent scopes come next: those more than twice their max interval since their last review, most overdue first by days over interval.

Every other scope gets score = days since its last review / its max interval + min(churn since then / its churn cap, 1) + 0.5 x min(open P0 and P1 findings, 2), rounded to three places, highest first.
Ties go to the lower scope id.
value.pick: Take the first scopes_per_window scopes the approved schedule allows.
value.overdue: A scope is overdue when its days since review exceed its max interval, and urgent when they exceed twice it.
value.no_starving: However busy other scopes are, a scope becomes urgent once it is twice its interval past its last review, and urgent scopes go before every other scope that has been reviewed. When a window's slots cover the scopes that come due, every scope is reviewed within about twice its interval; when they do not, the coverage review shows it and a person widens the window.
value.churn: Changed lines under a repository path, changed page digests for a site page, or changed renders for a video segment, since the last review.

value.title: Sorting this run's findings against the last run's
value.category_reason: A zero-call rule: the same two runs always sort the same way.
value.match_by: The findings to fixes fingerprint, so a finding keeps its identity across runs.

seen_now.still_open: Seen by the last run and again now, with no verified fix.
seen_now.reopened: Closed as resolved before, or open with a fix a different worker verified, and seen again now: the fix did not hold and its guard missed it.
seen_now.decided: Closed before by a person's decision, as won't fix or duplicate, and seen again: listed under decided_seen with that decision, never reopened or proposed for a fix.

not_seen_now.not_checked: Its check did not run this time, or the check's version changed since the last run; it stays open.
not_seen_now.fixed: A fix is recorded and a worker other than the fixer verified it.
not_seen_now.gone_unverified: A fix is recorded but not yet verified by another worker.
not_seen_now.gone_unexplained: No fix is recorded; it may be hidden, moved or intermittent.

value.first_run: The first run of a scope, and only that run, carries nothing from a previous run: every finding is new.

value.title: Record checks for review runs, with made-up golden runs
value.category_reason: Deterministic checks with made-up known-good and known-bad records; the validator recomputes every verdict.
value.purpose: Checks every review run must pass before it is appended to the log: the pinned scope and exact version, a person's approval for a scheduled run or a named requester for a manual one, the run it is compared with, checks that ran with their outputs and checks that did not with reasons, and every finding sorted with its follow-up: new ones recorded, fixed ones verified by someone other than the fixer, unverified and unexplained ones given a verification or a reproduction, unchecked ones kept open and reopened ones naming the closing they undid. The two made-up good runs pass; each made-up bad one fails exactly the one check named in fails.

deterministic_checks.why: The run pins the exact scope it reviewed.
The run names the exact version it reviewed.
A scheduled run names the person's approval it ran under.
A manual run names who asked for it.
A run that is not the first names the run it is compared with.
A first run carries nothing from a previous run, so it cannot hide findings by calling itself first.
Every check that ran gives its result and the digest of its output, so a claimed run traces to what it produced.
A check marked not run, skipped or unknown is listed under checks_not_run, never among the checks that ran.
Every check that did not run says why.
A finding is fixed only with a fix, a verification and who verified it.
The worker that made a fix never verifies it.
A fix nobody verified yet carries its proposed verb, verify-fix by the diff rules; diff-against-last-run's acceptance recomputes which.
A finding gone with no fix carries its proposed verb, reproduce by the diff rules.
A finding whose check did not run stays open, naming the check.
A reopened finding names the closing or verification it undid and its next verb, triage by the diff rules.
